sources.quote: Mortgage Professionals Canada's 2026 research found 38% of recent homebuyers arranged their mortgage through a broker, up about six points in a year, and 48% of first-time buyers
sources.title: Canadians increasingly turning to mortgage brokers for advice, not just rates: MPC survey
sources.evidence: 38% of recent homebuyers obtained their mortgage through a broker, up six percentage points from 2024, while the share rose to 48% among recent first-time buyers, an increase of 10 percentage points. The findings are included in MPC's latest report, The Broker Advantage: How Canadians Are Navigating Mortgage Choices in a More Complex Market.

sources.quote: Roughly 83% of broker clients said they would recommend theirs, a five-year high in that survey, and about 72% would use one again
sources.title: Mortgage broker share rises to 38%, hits 48% among recent first-time buyers: MPC - CMT News
sources.evidence: Access to the best rate remained the leading reason for using a broker, cited by 54% of respondents, while 33% pointed to receiving multiple quotes. Additionally, 83 per cent of broker clients said they would recommend their broker to a friend or family member — a five-year high — while 72% said they would use a broker again for their next mortgage.

sources.quote: Ontario licenses mortgage agents at two levels, and FSRA reserves private mortgages, mortgage investment corporations and syndicated mortgages for Level 2 agents and brokers
sources.publisher: Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA)
sources.title: New mortgage agent and broker licensing requirements | Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario
sources.evidence: As of April 1, 2023, mortgage agents and brokers are issued the mortgage agent level 1, level 2, and broker licences. The mortgage agent level 1 licence authorizes licensees to deal and trade in mortgages exclusively with lenders that are financial institutions, as defined in section 1 of the MBLAA, or approved by CMHC under the NHA. A mortgage agent level 2 may arrange mortgages with lenders which are financial institutions, approved lenders under the National Housing Act, as described in regulation and all other mortgage lenders (including mortgage investment companies, syndicates, private individuals, agents, brokers and brokerages).

sources.quote: Google's financial products policy requires advertiser verification in a growing list of regions
sources.title: Financial products and services - Advertising Policies Help
sources.evidence: You're required to complete a verification process to advertise financial services in some locations, which usually involves providing information about the type of services you provide, the licenses you hold to provide those services, your registration numbers, and any other relevant information about your business. Google requires verification for advertisers, with a separate verification needed for each targeted location.

sources.quote: Mortgage brokerage moved under the AMF and the Act respecting the distribution of financial products and services on May 1, 2020
sources.title: AMF is now supervising mortgage brokerage | AMF
sources.evidence: As of May 1, 2020, mortgage brokerage became a sector governed under the Act respecting the distribution of financial products and services (the Distribution Act) and regulated by the AMF. Up until April 30, 2020, mortgage brokerage was supervised by the Organisme d'autoréglementation du courtage immobilier du Québec (OACIQ).

sources.quote: with maximum penalties of $10 million per violation for organizations
sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation | CRTC
sources.evidence: The maximum amount of an administrative monetary penalty (AMP) per violation for an individual is $1 million, and for a business it is $10 million.

sources.quote: The Mortgage Services Act comes into force October 13, 2026, replacing the Mortgage Brokers Act with new disclosure obligations
sources.title: Mortgage Services Act | BCFSA
sources.evidence: The Mortgage Services Act (MSA) will come into force on October 13, 2026, at which time it will repeal and replace the outdated Mortgage Brokers Act (MBA), modernizing the regulation of B.C.'s mortgage services industry to provide greater consumer protection. On July 14, 2025, the BC Government approved the rules and regulation that accompany the MSA.

sources.quote: the minimum qualifying rate is the greater of 5.25% or the contract rate plus two points
sources.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI)
sources.title: OSFI maintains Minimum Qualifying Rate for uninsured mortgages - Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
sources.evidence: OSFI announced that the minimum qualifying rate for uninsured residential mortgages (MQR) will remain the greater of 5.25 per cent or the mortgage contract rate plus 2 per cent.

sources.quote: Since November 21, 2024, OSFI no longer expects it on uninsured straight switches at renewal where loan amount and amortization are unchanged
sources.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI)
sources.title: OSFI exempts uninsured mortgage straight switches from the prescribed MQR and implements portfolio LTI limits - Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
sources.evidence: Effective November 21, 2024, OSFI no longer prescribes the minimum qualifying rate (MQR) that it expects federally regulated financial institutions to apply when uninsured mortgage borrowers switch to a new institution at renewal. An uninsured straight switch refers to a mortgage with no increases in the remaining contractual mortgage amortization period or the loan amount.

sources.quote: The national 90 day mortgage delinquency rate reached 0.24% in the fourth quarter of 2025, up from 0.21% a year earlier and still below pre-pandemic levels
sources.title: Renewal wave peaks but still dominates mortgage market | CMHC
sources.evidence: The national 90+ day delinquency rate edged up to 0.24% in fourth quarter of 2025, up from 0.21% a year earlier but still below pre-pandemic levels. Renewal volumes are expected to ease through 2026, due to the large number of 3–5-year mortgages originated at lower interest rates in the early 2020s now reaching the end of their terms.
